subject: B-47 bomber coast
title: What If the Air Force Lost a Hydrogen Bomb? It Did in 1958. It's Still Missing

scenes.text: What if the Air Force lost a hydrogen bomb and never found it? Georgia, 1958.
scenes.keywords: b-47 bomber flying georgia coast aerial

scenes.text: February 5th, 1958. A B-47 bomber collided with an F-86 fighter during a night training exercise.
The damaged bomber jettisoned a 7,600-pound Mark 15 bomb into the sea near Tybee Island, then landed safely.
scenes.keywords: bomb bay doors runway landing lights

scenes.text: A hundred Navy divers searched for more than two months. On April 16th the bomb was declared irretrievably lost.
A 2004 search found only natural radiation from minerals. The Air Force says the plutonium core had been removed. A 1966 memo said otherwise.
The United States admits 32 accidents with nuclear weapons. Six of those weapons are still missing, somewhere under water and silt.

description:
What if the Air Force lost a hydrogen bomb? On 5 February 1958 a B-47 collided with an F-86 over Georgia and jettisoned a 7,600-pound Mark 15 bomb into Wassaw Sound off Tybee Island. A search of more than two months found nothing, and it was declared irretrievably lost on 16 April 1958.
A 2004 search found only naturally radioactive minerals. The US acknowledges 32 Broken Arrow accidents, and six weapons were never recovered.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: A 2001 Air Force report said the bomb is probably buried in 5 to 15 feet of silt and is safer left there. Would you want them to dig it up? And what should we run through next?
